query: Are there particular sectors I should reduce as I approach retirement, and which ones should I keep for income generation?

recommendations.title: Reduce Technology and Healthcare Sector Concentration
recommendations.summary: Decrease exposure to Technology (18%) and Healthcare (22%) sectors to reduce volatility as you enter your retirement glide path, targeting 10-12% each.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: At 55 with a 10-year retirement horizon, you should begin reducing concentration in growth-oriented sectors. Healthcare at 22% and Technology at 18% represent 40% of your portfolio—higher volatility sectors that, while valuable, pose unnecessary sequence-of-returns risk. Healthcare has regulatory and drug approval risks; Technology faces valuation compression risks. Your advanced experience allows you to execute this gradually over 2-3 years. Trim positions in UNH and any tech-heavy ETF components, redeploying to more defensive sectors while maintaining some exposure for inflation protection.
recommendations.suggested_action: Reduce Technology to 12% and Healthcare to 15% over next 18-24 months through systematic rebalancing

recommendations.title: Increase Consumer Staples and Utilities for Dividend Income
recommendations.summary: Boost Consumer Staples from 10% to 15% and add Utilities sector (currently 0%) at 8-10% for reliable dividend income and defensive characteristics.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Consumer Staples (PG currently at 10%) and Utilities are ideal retirement sectors: low volatility, consistent dividends, recession-resistant, and essential services. These sectors typically yield 2.5-4% dividends with modest growth. PG is excellent but you need diversification. Add positions in utilities ETFs (XLU) or individual utilities, and increase staples exposure through additional holdings like KO, CL, or KMB. These sectors historically outperform during market downturns and early retirement years when sequence risk is highest. With $220k income and low debt, you can afford gradual transition without tax concerns.
recommendations.suggested_action: Increase Consumer Staples to 15% and establish 8-10% Utilities position using dividends and proceeds from sector reductions

recommendations.title: Maintain Financials Exposure for Income and Inflation Protection
recommendations.summary: Keep Financials at current 18% allocation with JPM and BRK.B providing strong dividend growth and rising rate benefits.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your 18% Financials allocation through quality holdings (JPM, BRK.B) is appropriate for retirement income. Banks benefit from higher-for-longer interest rates, providing dividend growth that helps offset inflation. JPM yields ~2.5% with strong dividend growth history and fortress balance sheet. BRK.B offers unique diversification across sectors with minimal correlation to market swings—essentially a diversified portfolio within your portfolio. Financials offer better yield than tech/healthcare while maintaining moderate growth potential. This sector provides crucial inflation protection without excessive risk, perfectly suited for your moderate risk tolerance and medium-term horizon.
recommendations.suggested_action: Maintain current 18% allocation; no changes needed

recommendations.title: Reduce Energy Sector Exposure from 8% to 3-5%
recommendations.summary: Trim volatile Energy sector holdings to lower risk and reduce commodity price exposure as you approach retirement.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Energy at 8% is elevated for a retirement glide path investor. While energy provides inflation hedge and current income through dividends, it's highly cyclical and commodity-dependent with significant geopolitical risk. Price swings of 20-40% annually are common—inappropriate for sequence-of-returns risk management. At 55, you need stability over commodity beta. Reduce to 3-5% as satellite position for some inflation protection, but not core holding. Your moderate risk tolerance (loss comfort 5/10) and stable income suggest you don't need energy's volatility. Redeploy proceeds to Utilities and Consumer Staples recommendations above, improving income quality while reducing portfolio standard deviation.
recommendations.suggested_action: Reduce Energy allocation from 8% to 4% over next 12 months
